title: Differential Evolution of Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Profiles in Harbour and Coastal Sediments During Gran Tarajal Oil Spill Recovery: Implications for Bioremediation
content: Five campaigns (March–September 2018) monitored sediment PAH composition following the Gran Tarajal Harbour oil spill (Canary Islands, Spain), comparing 16 EPA priority PAHs and a nine-compound OSPAR subset. Harbour sediments, where specialised allochthonous bacteria were repeatedly applied, were compared with external stations without direct bioaugmentation. Initial PAH profiles differed between areas before treatment, potentially reflecting hydrocarbon transport and preferential sediment deposition; sampling configurations also differed between the first and subsequent campaigns. In the harbour, four- to six-ring PAHs increased from 56.54% to 73.60% of Σ16PAH between March and May; outside, their contribution fell from 75.74% to 9.71% by April. A contrasting transition around fluoranthene (Fla) was observed: lighter PAHs generally declined in relative abundance inside the harbour, whereas pyrene (Pyr) and heavier compounds increased; outside, the opposite tendency prevailed. Fla and Pyr followed different trajectories despite being structural isomers. The OSPAR subset increased from 70.40% to 87.06% of Σ16PAH inside between March and September but declined from 67.46% to 54.37% outside between March and April. Total hydrocarbon concentrations decreased markedly by September despite intervening fluctuations. The observed patterns may reflect microbial transformation, physicochemical processes and sediment transport; their individual contributions cannot be established from compositional data alone.
